summary: Steel fire tower on Mount Abram, Maine, built 1924; wrecked in 1925, destroyed by fire in 1949 and blown over in 2015. Listed gone; a 2019 account found it knocked over.

facts.design: Steel fire tower with a watchman's camp; 1924 items give 12 and 15 feet, a 1935 item 20 feet
facts.status_note: Blown over in 2015; a 2019 hiking account describes the summit tower as knocked over and caved in.

access.note: Part of the 6,214-acre Mt. Abraham Public Reserved Land; the Fire Warden's Trail is the usual route.

visit.trail_note: 4.5 miles to the summit on the Fire Warden's Trail, the most popular route

events.note: Steel bought in April 1924 for a 12-foot tower; a 15-foot steel tower was going up in July. The sources give different heights.
Ice-loaded tower crashed in December 1925 when a bolt on one of its four cables gave way; a watchman reported it.
A watchman was posted at the station in 1925.
A May 1935 item describes a 20-foot tower.
Found destroyed in May 1949 by a fire believed caused by lightning; the watchman was preparing for seasonal fire watch.
Watchman's camp removed in summer 2011; the state was still recommending removal of the tower.
Blown over in high winds and left lying on the summit; the only tower lost since the chapter's previous survey.
Hiking account describes the summit fire tower and shelter knocked over and caved in.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 3.7 (about 12 ft) is not confirmed by the sources read: the April 1924 item gives 12 ft, the July 1924 item 15 ft, and a 1935 item 20 ft; left out of facts. The record's 2015 'destroyed' event is recorded here as 'other' because the sources say the tower blew over and lay on the summit. The 1924-1949 newspaper items were read as transcriptions on the Eastern US lookouts site, not as the newspapers. The 1949 fire destroyed the tower of that date; the sources do not say when the tower standing in 2011 was built. The AllTrails page for the trail returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Access 'public' rests on the Maine by Foot description of public reserved land.
